evidence.quote: Owned intelligence is not the same as rented intelligence.

observations.why: The owned/rented opposition frames intelligence in proportionality terms — what you keep versus what you pay for — enacting market-pricing as a relational distinction.

evidence.quote: the perspective is the asset you keep

observations.why: Calling perspective an 'asset' casts it in cost-benefit, ROI terms — the commodity/asset split performs market-pricing proportionality.
Naming a 'thesis' positions the claim as a stance to be evaluated on its proportional merits, sustaining the market-pricing frame from the prior segments.
